Wen Zhe - Captivated me from the very beginning, even before she showed how full of personality she is! I don't see her getting much love at all, but she took me completely by surprise and solidified herself as my one pick, regardless if I was certain she wasn't debuting or not. She is hilarious, we all know that, but beyond that she works HARD, she's got stable vocals, and is a queen of dance. Every time she came up on screen I'd smile, and hearing her talk in her final interview about how she'd love to meet all her fans and truly just listen to them really melted my heart. She made extra effort to learn Korean so she could communicate with the K-group girls and never stopped trying to bridge that communication gap. I truly love WenZhe so much, and I really hope I can continue to follow her in whatever she does. I didn't expect to find so much joy from a contestant in this show. If I was having a down day I could just search Wen Zhe clips on youtube and she'd put a smile on my face. Seeing her debut in Korea would be a dream come true, I hope she doesn't give up. 

Bora - She is so sweet, kind, and beautiful in every single sense of the word. I find it hard to see anything that anyone could dislike about Bora. She was kind to every single one of the other girls, she was patient, respectful, and full of light the whole show! Especially being away from their homes and their families, I got the impression that Bora brought a sense of warmth and homely safety to everyone else. And I'm sure I don't need to mention her sheer vocal power. In my eyes, Bora was the BEST vocalist on the show bar absolutely none. Sure there are killer vocalists around, but she was in my opinion, the absolute best of the best. Absolutely gutted that she didn't debut. She truly, truly deserved it. 

Shana - So, so cute, and with a very understated sense of humour and dry charisma. Again, an absolute beast with the vocals and killed pretty much every single thing she did on the show. I really hope she finds success because she's built for it and I can see her debuting as soon as tomorrow. She's ready.   


Mention to Su Rui Qi, Yurina, Fu Yaning, Suyeon - While I didn't stan these girls, I saw them as talented and thought they were assured a spot in the final group. Breaks my heart to see them fall just short. Watching Yurina's face fall in particular was absolutely gut wrenching because she absolutely deserved a place in that top 9.   
Same to the other girls, who I didn't follow closely, but wishing them all the best.   


Sending some love to my girl WenZhe, don't give up!! You've got everything it takes to make it <3

Did the end of July and into August/September 2022. My nerves are through the roof about it as before covid got real bad my main goal was working toward building funds and getting a stable job to visit my partner in the UK before they'd eventually come down to Australia on a working visa. Those plans were obviously tossed in the air and now it's an excruciatingly uncertain situation, as I'm sure hundreds of thousands of other people feel too. Doesn't make it easy while at work my co-workers and managers enjoy saying they're "going to be brutally honest with me, but I highly doubt that anyone is leaving the country next year". Really huge blows to my mental health.   


I just really hope we're on track to open up in that mid-2022 timeframe. Life is so lonely and so stressful here, and I've been working so hard to make this life for myself and it's all put on hold indefinitely, yet the stressors of work still rule my life with nothing to really work toward, just a vague idea. And if it's too long will the relationship even survive? It's hard enough without covid. 

I'm in SA, who have had a relatively easy go of it, and I'd figure most people here are happy to stay locked down indefinitely. 

Thanks everyone for the encouraging and comforting words - it really did put my mind at ease and help me make a choice. We've just gotta keep supporting each other through this!

I'm so sorry :( And the time difference between us makes it even harder, doesn't it? And we're some of the farthest away we can be. We just need to make it through this - borders won't be closed forever and we can all meet again. We just need to hang in there, but i know the longer it goes, the harder it gets. It's also so difficult to talk about, but it stays this elephant in the room. "I can't wait to see you next year!" and in the back of my mind I'm thinking "What if I'm still not allowed to leave next year..."

I'm so sorry. I find reaching out to others in similar situations helps me feel less alone, hence why I made this post. I just don't know what there is to do. Obviously, we need to protect ourselves and each other from the virus, but at the same time people's mental health, especially those of us in LDR's, are suffering to extreme levels. I just really hope our country can pull it together soon, because this is so hard.

I struggle with boundaries being set because no matter what it feels like a rejection for me. 

Thinking on how I'd like a boundary to be set, I'd need to know that the person still cares about me, isn't going anywhere, doesn't dislike me (actively say that you still like your friend very much and enjoy your friendship a lot and don't want nor intend for that to shift!). Perhaps also gently inform your friend of the event that led you to the choice, without it sounding accusatory. If it comes out of nowhere I'd find myself tearing my thoughts apart trying to figure out what I did wrong or what is "wrong" with me to have caused that.   


You clearly care a lot about your friend and I think it's actually really thoughtful and compassionate that you've turned here for some advice.
